Long before the sleek ships of the Empire ruled the Silver Currents, before its golden cathedrals rose from the salt and stone, the land of Falkini was said to be nothing more than a barren spit of earth  a graveyard for the unworthy and a haven for the mad. The winds were harsh, the soil cursed, and the seas forever in turmoil. Yet from this desolation, legend says, the Gods distilled perfection.
The Birth of the Empire
They say the first Falkinians were castaways  survivors of a storm that lasted thirteen moons. Their ship, The Saint Maruna, shattered on the black reefs, spilling its rum casks into the sea. When the survivors crawled ashore, the seafoam turned amber, and a voice rose from the depths  deep as thunder, smooth as honey:
From my blood you shall drink, and from my wrath you shall rule.
The voice was that of Rumael, the Sea God of Tempests and Temptation. He offered the castaways a covenant: eternal endurance in exchange for devotion  and the promise that no storm would ever take them again if they drank of his Sacred Rum.
They agreed. And as the first cask was raised to their lips, the barren land beneath them began to pulse with life. Palms sprouted overnight, the waves calmed, and gold shimmered beneath the black sands. Thus was born The Holy Empire of Falkini  land of rum, resilience, and divine rebellion.
The Curse of the Dogs
The empires national animal, the Falkinian Dog, was said to have been created by Rumael himself. Legend tells that he plucked the soul of a drowned sailor and bound it into a beast loyal to humankind but ever longing for the sea.
Each dog bore eyes the color of deep rum and fur that glimmered like wet sand. It was said that when a Falkinian died at sea, their spirit would take the shape of one of these dogs, running along the coasts under the full moon, howling until the tide claimed them once more.
But when the Empire began cutting down its forests for ships, burning sacred groves for lumber, the Dogs began to vanish  one by one, until their howls became rare as pearls in the dust. Fishermen whisper that when the last Dog dies, Rumael will return, and with him, a storm that will never end.
The Spirits Beneath the Gold
Deep beneath the Empires uranium mines  now symbols of progress and power  miners speak of strange drums echoing through the stone. The sound is not metal nor machine, but the heartbeat of the Drowned King, Rumaels son, chained below for betraying his fathers covenant.
They say he once tried to lead the Falkinians away from divine servitude, offering them freedom from Rumaels control. In fury, the Sea God struck him down, sealing his body in the mineral veins of the earth  where his sorrow turned to gold, and his rage to uranium.
Every few years, the miners discover veins that glow faintly blue, pulsing like living flesh. The oldest among them cross themselves and whisper,
The Drowned King still dreams. Pray he does not wake.
The Shadow of the Corporates
In the high towers of Falkinis capital, the CEOs and priests drink the same vintage of sacred rum, each claiming their authority comes from divine will. But sailors, smugglers, and mystics alike say that the corporations are not mere men  they are vessels, bodies possessed by fragments of Rumaels essence.
It is said the first Chairman drank so deeply from the Sea Gods cask that his soul split in two  half human, half divine. Now, each generation of the corporate elite undergoes a secret ceremony in the underwater vaults beneath the city, where they drink from that same ancient barrel. Those who survive emerge cold-eyed, smooth-tongued, and utterly loyal to the will of the tide.
The Eternal Storm Prophecy
Old seers of Falkini tell that one day, the Empire will drink too deeply of its own prosperity. The gold will turn to salt, the uranium to ash, and the last Falkinian Dog will howl beneath a red moon. When that night comes, the ocean will rise and whisper the forgotten name of Rumael.
And from the depths will emerge The Rum Tide  a flood of amber waves swallowing ships, cities, and even the mountains. But amid the chaos, one soul  a child born under the crest of the drowned moon  will carry the Eternal Cask, and with it, the power to either renew or end the covenant forever.
Todays Whisper
Now, when sailors dock in Falkinis rum-soaked ports, they still pour a single drop of their drink into the sea before they take their first sip.
Not for superstition.
Not for thanks.
But for fear.
For they know the ocean remembers  and so does Rumael.
